gap: No result ChatGPT got states, from the makers' own documents, the moving-coil (MC) load each shortlisted amp gives a cartridge, or the Marantz matching rule. The Marantz MODEL 30 is the only one with a switchable MC load (33 / 100 / 390 Ω, and Marantz says to use MC LOW for cartridges under 50 Ω, MID for about 50 Ω and HIGH for 100 Ω or more). The Luxman L-505Z has a fixed 100 Ω load, the Musical Fidelity A1 has a fixed 1 kΩ nominal load, and the Rega Elex Mk4 takes moving-magnet (MM) cartridges only.
standout_why: Rival pages I opened: rhythmaudio.com (Darko on the L-505Z) says only that the phono stage was tried with two MC setups and gives no load or gain figures. luxman.com detail.php?id=49 (cited) already lists the L-505Z MC input as 0.3 mV / 100 Ω, so that one cell is not new. ChatGPT's own answer already says the Elex Mk4 is MM-only and that the MODEL 30 has 'multiple MC settings', but it gives no ohm values, no matching rule and no A1 load. I couldn't read three rivals. The What Hi-Fi best-amplifiers page and the Elex Mk4 review both returned only their titles. Stereophile's Recommended Components page returned HTTP 403. Their coverage of MC loading is unchecked, so I've scored this as partial rather than new.
decides: This confirms the MODEL 30 as the MC pick and makes the reason concrete: it is the only candidate whose MC load can be set to suit the cartridge's internal impedance. Low-impedance MC cartridges get 33 Ω and cartridges of 100 Ω or more get 390 Ω. The L-505Z (fixed 100 Ω) and the A1 (fixed 1 kΩ) give every MC cartridge the same load. An MC owner looking at the Elex Mk4 needs a separate MC phono stage, because Rega's page lists only an MM phono stage.

findings.label: MC input impedance settings and the maker's matching rule
findings.value: MM; MC LOW 33 Ω (cartridges under 50 Ω); MC MID 100 Ω (cartridges of about 50 Ω); MC HIGH 390 Ω (cartridges of 100 Ω or more)
findings.source_title: Marantz MODEL 30 online manual: Cartridge selector
findings.note: Marantz: pick the setting closest to the cartridge maker's recommended load, 'or select a value a few times that of the cartridge's internal impedance'. Sound returns about 4 s after the setting is changed. This is the EU/EN manual; I found no US-specific spec page.

findings.label: Phono input sensitivity / impedance
findings.value: MM 2.3 mV / 39 kΩ; MC 250 µV at 33 Ω, 100 Ω or 390 Ω; RIAA deviation ±0.5 dB (20 Hz–20 kHz)
findings.note: The same page gives rated power as 100 W × 2 into 8 Ω (1 kHz, 0.05% THD) and 200 W × 2 into 4 Ω.

findings.label: Phono input sensitivity / impedance
findings.value: MM 2.5 mV / 47 kΩ; MC 0.3 mV / 100 Ω, a fixed load (no selectable MC load is listed)
findings.note: Luxman calls the stage 'MM/MC compatible'. ChatGPT cited this page.

findings.label: Phono cartridge type supported
findings.value: MM only: 'integrated moving magnet (MM) phono stage'; no MC input
findings.note: Rega's page lists 1 MM phono input, 4 line inputs, 1 optical and 1 coaxial digital input (32–192 kHz, 16–24 bit), and no USB. Phono input impedance and capacitance are not listed. For MC, Rega's page points to its separate Fono MC phono stage.

findings.label: Phono input specs per mode
findings.value: MM 5 mV / 50 kΩ / 100 pF / 40 dB gain; MC 450 µV / 1 kΩ nominal ('automatic input impedance matching') / 60 dB gain
findings.note: One shared phono input switched between MM and MC. Signal-to-noise is 75 dB (MM) and 70 dB (MC). The page lists no user-selectable MC load. This is the maker's global page, not a US store page.

unsourced: Yamaha A-S1200 phono MM/MC sensitivity and impedance, and whether its MC load is fixed.
